headline: MacKinnon (lower-body) will play in Game 4 in Vegas.
news: MacKinnon left Game Three on Sunday late in the second period after suffering a lower-body injury. He returned early in the third period, but was used sparingly, spending most of the final frame on the bench. It's unclear if he will be able to return to his usual playing capacity in Game Four, but his presence will nevertheless be a positive sign for an Avalanche team trying to stave off elimination.

headline: Kaprizov (undisclosed) will play Sunday vs. the Blue Jackets.
Guentzel (rest) will not play against the Rangers on Wednesday.
Nylander (illness) is on the ice for warmups; he's expected to play vs. the Sharks.
Oettinger will start in Washington on Tuesday.
news: The Stars have struggled offensively this season, but are off to a solid 8-5-1 record thanks to strong netminding from Jake Oettinger. The 27-year-old American goalie was solid in his most recent outing, saving 24 of 25 shots (.960 SV%) in a 3-1 win over the Columbus Blue Jackets. In his last 10 games (7-2-1), he has a dazzling 1.58 GAA and a .923 SV%. The Stars enter Tuesday's outing as slight -102 road underdogs against a Washington Capitals team coming off a 5-1 loss to the Minnesota Wild.

headline: Schaefer (illness) will play vs. New Jersey on Tuesday.
news: Schaefer was absent from practice on Monday due to illness, but he attended the team's morning skate on Tuesday and will be in the lineup in the evening against the New Jersey Devils. The 18-year-old rookie's tremendous season continued in the Islanders' most recent game, recording two goals, including the overtime winner, in a 4-3 victory over the Toronto Maple Leafs. He has 28 points (12G / 16A) in 42 games this season.

headline: Marner (personal) returned to practice on Monday.
news: Marner has missed the past two games, tending to a personal matter, but was back at practice on Monday and will likely be back in the lineup on Tuesday against the Ottawa Senators. The 29-year-old Marner is off to a strong start this season, with 12 points (2G / 10A) in 11 games.

headline: Bedard (shoulder) is expected to make his season debut vs. Pittsburgh on Tuesday.
news: Bedard missed all of training camp and the opening six games of the season, but he should make his debut on Tuesday against the Pittsburgh Penguins. The Blackhawks can't afford to go much longer without their 21-year-old superstar after scoring just 12 goals in their first six games (1-5-0). Bedard had 30 goals, 75 points and 226 SOG in 69 GP last season.

headline: Heiskanen (upper body) is doubtful for Saturday vs. San Jose.
news: Heiskanen was limited to 9:41 of ice time in Tuesday's 6-5 win over the Washington Capitals and left with an upper-body injury. Thomas Harley saw an increased role and deployment on the top powerplay unit, which should continue on Saturday. That said, Heiskanen will likely be ready for the Stars following game on Thursday against the Winnipeg Jets.

headline: Point (rest) will not play against the Rangers on Wednesday.
2-year, $18,000,000 contract with the Vegas Golden Knights. Breakdown to be confirmed . Expires 2029 (UFA).
Blake (rest) is expected to be back in the Hurricanes' lineup on Monday.
news: With Carolina locking up their playoff position over the weekend, Jackson Blake found himself out of the lineup due to rest related purposes but will draw back into the lineup vs. Philadelphia on Monday. The 22-year-old forward has taken a massive step forward in his second NHL season, picking up career highs in goals (22), assists (30), points (52), PIMs (40) and SOG (167) through 79 games played.

headline: Podkolzin (illness) will play vs. Philadelphia on Saturday.
Lafreniere (illness) is expected to play vs. Buffalo on Thursday.
news: The Rangers are battling a myriad of key injuries and had a scare on Wednesday when Lafreneiere was absent from practice because of an illness, but he should play on Thursday against the Buffalo Sabres. The 24-year-old Lafreniere has been held off the scoresheet in 28 of 44 games this season and continues to be unable to live up to the expectations he garnered when he was drafted first overall in the 2020 NHL Entry Draft. He has 24 points (9G / 15A) in 44 games this season.

headline: Stankoven (illness) missed practice on Thursday.
news: Stankoven is battling an illness and did not practice on Thursday, but will be hopeful to play when Carolina opens the postseason on Saturday. Stankoven has been an effective offensive contributor in his previous two postseasons and hopes to carry his late-season momentum into a deep playoff run for the Hurricanes. The 23-year-old has nine points (7G / 2A) during a six-game point streak.

headline: Jarry (illness) is expected to back up vs. Anaheim on Thursday.
news: The Oilers have leaned on Jarry since Devon Levi suffered a lower-body injury two weeks ago, but they will turn to Matt Tomkins on Thursday, as Jarry is battling an illness. The 31-year-old Jarry will still serve as the backup. He has a 2.57 GAA and .902 SV% in eight games (4-1-3).

headline: 3-year, $9,750,000 contract with the New Jersey Devils. Expires 2029 (UFA).
Cowan is expected to return to Toronto lineup on Saturday vs. Ottawa.
The Lightning have signed John Carlson to a two-year deal worth $8.5M AAV ($17.0M total).
news: The Carolina Hurricanes acquired John Carlson's rights from the Anaheim Ducks earlier in the offseason, but he decided to test the open marketing, ultimately opting two sign a two-year contract with the Tampa Bay Lightning. With Darren Raddysh's departure from Tampa Bay, Carlson could be an option to fill the void on the team's top powerplay unit. The 36-year-old Carlson had a terrific 2025-26 season, split between the Washington Capitals and Anaheim Ducks, scoring 60 points (14G / 46A) in 71 games.

headline: Stolarz will start vs. Vancouver on Saturday.
news: Stolarz allowed two goals on 32 shots in the Maple Leafs' win in Edmonton last Saturday. Sergei Bobrovsky has started the last two games, but Stolarz will make his sixth start of the season in Vancouver. He's played well so far, going 4-1-0 with a 2.79 GAA and .907 SV%, and draws a great matchup as -181 road favourites.

headline: D'Astous will draw into the lineup on Saturday.
